question.text: Given that $(x+3)$ and $(x-1)$ are factors of $f(x) = ax^3+7x^2+bx-9,$ then $a+b=$
question.explanation:
According to the factor theorem, if $(x-r)$ is a factor of $f(x),$ then the root $x = r$ is also a root of $f(x).$

Here, we are considering the factors $(x+3)$ and $(x-1).$ The roots of these factors can be found by setting the factors equal to $0$ and solving:

\begin{align} x+3 = 0 &\quad \Rightarrow \quad x= -3 \\ x-1 = 0 &\quad \Rightarrow \quad x= 1 \end{align}

According to the factor theorem, then, since $(x+3)$ and $(x-1)$ are factors of $f(x),$ the roots $x=-3$ and $x=1$ are also roots of $f(x).$ This means $f(-3)=0$ and $f(1)=0,$ so we have \begin{align} f(-3) & = 0\\[3pt] a(-3)^3 + 7(-3)^2 + b(-3) - 9 & = 0\\[3pt] -27a - 3b + 63 - 9 & = 0\\[3pt] -27a - 3b & = -54\\[3pt] -9a - b & = -18, \\ \\ f(1) & = 0\\[3pt] a(1)^3 + 7(1)^2 + b(1) - 9 & = 0\\[3pt] a + b + 7 - 9 & = 0\\[3pt] a + b & = 2. \end{align}

This gives a system of equations

\[ \begin{cases} -9a - b = -18 \\ a+b = 2. \end{cases} \]

Adding the equations, we eliminate $b$ and get

\[ -8a = -16\quad\Rightarrow\quad a=2. \]

Substituting $a=2$ in either equation gives $b=0.$ So our solutions are $a=2$ and $b=0.$ Finally then,

\[ a+b = 2+0 = 2. \]

question.explanation:
According to the factor theorem, if $(x - r)$ is a factor of $p(x),$ then the root $x = r$ is also a root of $p(x).$

Here, we are considering the factor $(x+5).$ The root of this factor can be found by setting the factor equal to $0$ and solving: \begin{align} x + 5 & = 0\\ x & = -5 \end{align}

According to the factor theorem, then, since $(x+5)$ is a factor of $p(x),$ the root $x = -5$ is also a root of $p(x).$ This means $p \left( -5 \right) = 0,$ so we have \begin{align} p(-5) & = 0\\[3pt] 3(-5)^2 + 14(-5) + c & = 0\\[3pt] 75 - 70 + c & = 0\\[3pt] c & = -5. \end{align}

question.text: Given that $(2x-1)$ and $(x+2)$ are factors of $f(x)=a x^3 + b x^2 - 2 x$, then $a+b=$
question.explanation:
According to the factor theorem, if $(x-r)$ is a factor of $f(x),$ then the root $x = r$ is also a root of $f(x).$

Here, we are considering the factors $(2x-1)$ and $(x+2).$ The roots of these factors can be found by setting the factors equal to $0$ and solving:

\begin{align} 2x-1 = 0 &\quad \Rightarrow \quad x= \dfrac{1}{2} \\[5pt] x+2 = 0 &\quad \Rightarrow \quad x= -2 \end{align}

According to the factor theorem, then, since $(2x-1)$ and $(x+2)$ are factors of $f(x),$ the roots $x=\dfrac{1}{2}$ and $x=-2$ are also roots of $f(x).$ This means $f\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=0$ and $f(-2)=0,$ so we have

\begin{align*} f\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) &= 0 \\[5pt] a\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3 + b \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 - 2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) & = 0\\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{8}a + \dfrac{1}{4}b - 1 & = 0\\[5pt] a +2b - 8 & = 0\\[5pt] a + 2b & = 8,\\ \\ f(-2) &= 0 \\[5pt] a (-2)^3 + b (-2)^2 - 2 (-2) & = 0\\[5pt] -8a + 4b + 4 & = 0\\[5pt] -8a + 4b & = -4 \\[5pt] 2a - b & = 1 . \end{align*}

This gives a system of equations

\[ \begin{cases} a + 2b = 8 \\[3pt] 2a - b = 1. \end{cases} \]

Eliminating $b,$ we get

\[ 5a = 10\quad\Rightarrow\quad a=2. \]

Substituting $a=2$ in either equation gives $b=3.$ So our solutions are $a=2$ and $b=3.$ Finally then, \[ a+b = 2+3 = 5. \]
